summary.one_liner: AgentGPT is a web-based platform for configuring, deploying, and running autonomous AI agents that break a user-given goal into tasks, execute them, and learn from results.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes AgentGPT as a way to name a custom AI agent, give it a goal, and have it reason toward that goal by planning tasks, executing them, and learning from the outcomes. It is presented as usable in the browser, with a hosted site offered for demo use. The project ships an automatic setup CLI (setup.sh for Mac/Linux, setup.bat for Windows) that configures environment variables and API keys, a MySQL database, a FastAPI backend, and a Next.js frontend. The stack is listed as Next.js 13 with TypeScript, FastAPI, Prisma and SQLModel, Next-Auth.js for auth, TailwindCSS with HeadlessUI, Zod and Pydantic for validation, and Langchain for LLM tooling. The README names an OpenAI API key as required and Serper and Replicate keys as optional.
use_cases: run an autonomous AI agent toward a custom goal
self-host a browser-based AI agent app
learn how a Next.js and FastAPI agent app is built
how_to_run: git clone the AgentGPT repository (URL left blank in the README)
Add the requested API keys when the setup script prompts for them
Wait for all services to start, then open the app in a web browser
notable: Automatic setup CLI that configures env vars, API keys, database, backend, and frontend
Browser-based interface for naming and deploying custom autonomous agents
Built on create-t3-app and a FastAPI template
Optional Serper and Replicate integrations alongside the required OpenAI key
caveats: Requires Docker and an OpenAI API key before the setup will run
Setup depends on several local tools (Node.js, Git, an editor) and is not a single-command install
The README does not state a license
keywords: run ai to reach a goal
ai that breaks goals into tasks
